mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations adjust downwards.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 declines and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 300,000 in a month, it signals strong labor market conditions, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and confidence rise.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% in a month, it signals weakening demand in the housing sector, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to broader economic concerns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between HOUST declines and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure in a tight monetary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction effect between FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a high level of real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) relative to GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings benefit.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between RSAFS/GDPC1 ratio and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
